paragraphs: Rabbi Yosta son of Rabbi Matun.

Zevachim 99a has Rabbi Yosta, son of Rabbi Matun, reporting Rabbi Yochanan. Yoma 30b reads Rabbi Dostai, son of Rabbi Matun; Hyman calls that a textual error because Dostai was a Tanna, as Berakhot 7b shows, and cites Dikdukei Soferim for the Yosta reading. In Jerusalem Talmud Bava Kamma 7:4, Rabbi Yosta, son of Rabbi Matun, asks a question and Resh Lakish objects.

notes.text: Hyman distinguishes the Amora Yosta from the Tanna Dostai. He does not identify the two simply because their names resemble each other.

The consulted Zevachim 99a has Yostai beRabbi Matun reporting Rabbi Yochanan; Yoma 30b has Dostai bar Matun reporting Rabbi Yochanan. Hyman’s correction and chronological distinction remain his argument. The exact Dikdukei Soferim reading was not independently inspected.
